name: dish_tokens
frozen: 2026-11-16, before any model call of the token and pipeline studies
question: What is the cheapest way to run the naive selection call without losing answer quality?

inputs.selection: 12 of the 27 well-formed inputs, random.Random(seed).sample over the sorted ids, fixed before any run of this study

variants.B: production prompt and schema, JSON user message with owned first, max_tokens 8192 (a ceiling, not a target); quality baseline
variants.V0: production settings as shipped (max_tokens 2048); expected to truncate
variants.V2: as B with a compact plain-text user message (owned ingredients and dish names comma-separated)
variants.V3: as B with the reasoning parameter set to disabled (reasoning: {enabled: false}); if the request is rejected the variant is recorded as unsupported
variants.V4: as B with a minimal schema {name, missing} (no 'have'); have_subset is not computed for this variant
variants.V5: as B with the dish list first and the owned ingredients last (static prefix first); cached tokens are read from the usage field

decision_rule: Take B's quality metrics as the baseline. A variant qualifies if it has zero truncated answers and every quality metric it has is within 2 percentage points below B's (higher is not penalised). Choose the qualifying variant with the lowest mean cost per call; ties go to the lower mean output tokens. The smallest max_tokens of V0/V1a/V1b/B with zero truncations on these inputs is recorded as the no-truncation setting.
limits: 12 inputs, single run at temperature 0: run-to-run variation is not measured
quality is consistency with the rule-made reference, not human-labelled
cached tokens depend on the provider and on calls arriving within the cache lifetime
